author: VLM
title: Renting is Throwing Money Away, Right? (2015)
body:
Not so, I bought the cheapest washing machine I could get. I dropped about $1200 cash on a speed queen that'll last me maybe 20 years. Joe 6 pack finances a new LG every three years at 29.99% credit card interest for $600 and thinks I'm getting ripped off.

Its just like the situation with hiking boots, I can only afford the $250 boots that last many years, I'm not rich enough to afford the $100 boots that only last one year before falling apart. I can't afford to spend $100, I have to spend $250. Richer people than I, can buy themselves the $100 boots.

Also at some big box stores I've seen some masterful post sale salesmanship. New washer hoses cost $19 on the shelf but as part of the installation package they'll prevent your basement from being flooded for only $50 installed by our professionals (usually lower quality hoses too). Installation "only" costs $99 but you need the new hoses for $50 and fuel prices went up a decade ago so we still have our temporary $19.99 fuel surcharge on our deliveries. Oh you want the old washer hauled away, thats only $50 and they totally take care of the problem for you. Technically according to google search you can buy a box containing a LG top loader thats normally $770 for a mere $650, but unless you have time, skills, and a large vehicle that box of machinery won't wash any clothes for $650, add something like $220 worth of installation... Oh and thats 18 months financing but it only has a one year guarantee for parts and labor, which is comical... for a mere $150 you can get a five year guarantee which is about a quarter the lifespan of my speed queen, if and only if you also purchase installation services. Suddenly that "cheap" $650 washer is going to hit the credit card for over a kilobuck and its only going to last five years at best while providing plenty of repair work headaches. So figure twenty years of clothes washing costs $1200 with a speed queen or over $4000 with LG products... I'm not wealthy enough to buy $650 washers I can only afford the $1200 washers.

author: drzaiusapelord
title: They Used To Last 50 Years
body:
Except its rare to see actual documented proof that this is a real practice in reputable industry. Sure it must happen (or seem to happen as a unintended effect), but from a rational perspective if Samsung does this then I'll switch to LG, thus costing Samsung business and reputation. I have no brand loyalty so it doesn't make sense to make unreliable products. I, like any consumer, get pissed off and I switch to other brands at the drop of a hat. I'll also address the article point by point:

> Motors last about 1/3 to 1/4 as long as they used to.

That's questionable, but lowered motor life is probably in the cards due to efficiency gains. Modern motors are far more efficient than old ones and the more efficient designs are simply more delicate for a variety of reasons not the least of it is lighter materials and running closer to their optimal maximum which means more wear and running hotter in general. Also the reduction of hazardous materials and other regulations means we can't just use environmentally dangerous materials like lead willy-nilly anymore. I recently read that due to laziness and consumer ignorance, your average ceiling fan was something like 30% efficient up until fairly recently. So you were burning a good 75-100 watts on what should have been 15-30watt usage. These manufacturers just used these old designs for decades, thus increasing our electric bills and adding to pollution. Consumers pick up the fan and feel its "heavy" due to this old motor and think its "quality." Its really just a waste of electricity.

>Not enough competition.

I just bought all new appliances for my house a few years back. If anything, I was bowled over by all the players in this space and had to do a lot of legwork in regards to reviews. I really don't think lack of competition is an issue.

>Refrigerator door seals are glued on now instead of screwed on

This is a generalization. For my current and previous fridge they were screwed on. Even then, strong glues could hold these for their expected two decade lifetime if done correctly. Again, the author can't, or won't, give us specifics here. Certainly cheap and poorly engineered brands exist. Name and shame. Don't generalize.

>They can often be found for $300 at big box retailers, but they usually break within 2-3 years.

10+ years on my last dishwasher before I moved and 4 in on my current one. No issues and my current one is a fairly low-end Samsung. I do ok financially, but I'm cheap. My samsung is a cheap knock-off of the 'real' Bosch at the store. It even mimmicks its styling. So yeah, I'm not buying rich guy stuff here. Also, we're parents so we run that thing almost everyday.

>There is too much confusion over who is making quality appliances.

10-20 minutes reading reviews isn't asking a lot. I spend more time reading reviews of office chairs or video games, let alone $500+ appliances I depend on for my daily living.

>Newer appliances start rusting within even a year or two whereas I’ve seen washers and dryers and other appliances from 40 years ago that are still rust free.

I can't remember the last time I saw rust on a modern appliance. Maybe this is limited to one vendor using cheap paint. I wish the author tried to be specific. Rust on the stuff I grew up with was everywhere. I remember trying hard not to cut my hand while doing the laundry. I remember my dad buying rustoliem all the time because everything rusted back then. We didn't have clear-coats as an industry norm and stainless steel, a mid-range finishing today, was rich guy and restaurant only stuff back then. We had nice thick but brittle paint, but if you chip that, and don't catch it on time, then you got rust.

> If an old refrigerator or freezer would last 40-50 years before being replaced

These were serious edge cases and as an old-timer I remember having a repair tech come out periodically and my parents paying fairly significant bills to fix this stuff. Sure they "lasted" only because we were constantly replacing their innards.

>Elon Musk would have already started working on building a better appliance that runs off a battery bank and solar.

If you think today's stuff is overly engineered and delicate, wait until you start dealing with the pita that li-ion batteries are and how short their effective lifetimes are with daily use. Let alone running solar and how much that'll cost to install within code on your roof and how much that'll increase the cost the next time you re-do your roof. I have cheap-ish electricity and natural gas available in my basement. I'm good, thanks.

Seriously, this guy isnt a researcher or engineer, he's some guy who sells junk on craiglist. This post is one step above 'forwards from grandma' territory. This is classic fallacy of idealizing the past here. I imagine as a craigslist junk seller he doesn't see the old appliances our parents all threw away, he's just seeing a biased sample of all the stuff that were well maintained or had low usage, like buying a 30 year old car with 20,000 miles and bemoaning how 'cheap and crappy' modern cars are.

That said, the modern world isn't all roses. Because there are so many more manufacturers and so many budget brands, its easy to cheap out and get a lemon. Or there are so many lines, its sometimes unfair when you get a lemon model from a decent manufacturer. When I was a kid these things cost, fixed for inflation, a whole hell of a lot of money. And even in the late 70s and early 80s, in a normal non-ghetto but not rich Chicago neighborhood, I still watched old ladies scrub their laundry on washboards and hang them on laundry lines because of cost prohibitive issues. You either could afford for the reliable $1,000 GE washer or you couldn't. Lets not romanticize a time where everything was super expensive and which left a lot of people out in the cold.

Some people are going to buy the budget Amana that is crappier than the GE they grew up with, but it regularly goes on sale/clearance for $250 or so at Walmart. Sure beats the $700+ GE if you're poor and very much beats paying the laundromat. The take away here isn't modern things are terrible, its don't buy budget brands if you want quality.

author: dbg31415
title: They Used To Last 50 Years
body:
You're describing Sears, no? Sarcasm doesn't read so well on the internet but yeah my parents still have a washing machine from probably 1970 in their house. The matching dryer finally gave up on them about 5 years back... that thing was still to this day the best dryer I ever used. Run it 30 minutes, even the heaviest towels were crispy dry and almost too hot to handle when you took them out.

I think having high quality appliances is partially why Sears tanked... First they didn't sell as many (due to having to compete on price with lower quality / cheaper products), then when they found a way to compete (having Samsung make Kenmore appliances, for example), they lost the quality and the last reason anyone would opt to go there over Costco or Amazon or Home Depot.

I bought a matching Washer / Dryer set from Costco. Then the next year I bought a Fridge and Dishwasher from LG there too. For the first three years or so it was fine, but about 5 years in I think they all have issues. My house is about 20 years old, and the Dishwasher I replaced was the original... so it lasted 15 years. I can say that the new (and fairly top of the line) Dishwasher has more issues at 5 than the old builder-grade one had at 15. I really regret not getting a Bosch...

But even up into the 80s and 90s Sears / Maytag were known for selling top quality goods that didn't break. Here's a cute commercial.

title: Cathode-Retro: A collection of shaders to emulate the display of an NTSC signal
body:
The vertical RGB shadow mask specifically wasn't unconsciously visible at normal viewing distance--usually only the raster lines were. On these screenshots, I can see and almost count horizontal pixels. This could also be because most shadow masks weren't the RGB stripes like most LCDs--the Trinitron was with a cylindrical CRT. The shadow mask was usually also more fine than the max resolution so there was no 1:1 (or 3:1) mapping to pixels as there is in this simulated display.

I don't mean wider color gamut, I mean that for lower intensities, the saturation can remain high. Most current IPS panels at lower intensities, the color saturation gets washed out (think DLP projector). This correlates with having deep AND distinguishable blacks. IPS has high brightness, VA has higher contrast ratios.

Because of this, I probably won't buy an IPS panel except for 'business' text use.

The LG/Dell Nano IPS Black (aka IPS Black and different than Nano IPS) is reported as being better--I haven't seen it in person so can't comment.

title: What is the future of the Internet of things? (over the next 10 years)
body:

Let suppose you are living in 2020 where all of your consumer electronics device are connected with each other. Your smartphones and home appliances like fridge, TV, AC etc .

Suppose its Sunday and you are doing you’re weekly shopping at your favorite shopping mall. Your refrigerator received your GPS location through your Smartphone and you received a notification of this kind on your Smartphone screen -

    20% milk remaining in the bottle
    Butter about to finish
    Fish will expire tomorrow
Awesome, isn’t it? Now you know that you have to purchase these items from store .

The above written lines are not a plain pridiction. They are based on the patent filings by various companies. All of the electronic equipment in your house will be connected with each other and will be communicating all necessary information. For example, your alarm clock will be shutting down your AC as soon as you will be leaving your bed in morning and will be saving electricity.

Even you car will be connected with your smartphones and other devices. You just have to send your GPS location information to your car via your smartphone and it will navigate to pick your from whereever you are present. The driverless car of Google will be doing this in future.

What do you think? Lets discuss

author: logfromblammo
title: All United Flights Grounded Due to Mysterious Problem
body:
They don't even need to go bankrupt. I have an LG television that has been promising new widgets ever since I first got it, and no new widget has ever appeared.

The impetus there was that LG changed its net-connected TV platform in 2011, and instantly dropped all support for older devices. One would think that a final update could remove that "coming soon" box from their proprietary added-feature screen, but they haven't even bothered to do that.

So I can watch NetFlix and YouTube on that device, but not Amazon instant video, or Crackle, or Crunchyroll, or Vimeo, or any of the dozens of selections available to better supported platforms. Having learned my lesson, and aware of the increasingly stalkerish behavior of "smart" televisions, my next TV purchase was very specifically a dumb screen. If I want an internet-connected service now, I use the Wii, or XBox, or the extended desktop from the nearest computer.

I will likely refuse to buy any network-enhanced appliance in the future, unless I am able to root/jailbreak it and install software without the manufacturer's stamp of approval. I probably wouldn't do much beyond installing ChillBox, or FridgeBSD, or CryogenMod, or whatever, but it feels like the possibility might keep them a little more honest. Because you know that refrigerator hackers would be capturing and picking apart every packet that thing sends out, quickly discovering that every time someone closes the door, it sends a tattle out to fridge-use.org about how long you stood there with the fridge door open, along with before-and-after photos of your food.

Though it would also be embarrassing if they marketed value models of a product line by disabling features in software/firmware, and some NetBSD-loving punks could come along and write a simple script that turns the doohickey that retails at $200 into the one that sells for $800.

So it's already too late for me. "Smart" appliances are just another low-capability computer that I will have to support as the in-home IT guy. And I will have to presume that they come pre-loaded with all manner of crapware and spyware. I would forever need to be checking on chipsets and revision numbers and compatibility lists. No thanks. It's hard enough managing the congestion on the home WiFi already.

author: poulsbohemian
title: The lifespan of large appliances is shrinking
body:
We've gone through three refrigerators in about four years...the first one had survived more than ten years and had just run its course -- all the cheap plastic had broken on it, but it still kept things cold. Replaced with a second-hand LG, and you know how that went - compressor went out after two years and would have cost as much as a new one to repair. Bought an outlet store domestic brand (I forget which one now) - freezer didn't work, back to the store it went. Bought a Kenmore (I think?)... turns out it is one of the models that has known issues, and the parts backlog is at least 6 months. Living in small town America, the problem is made worse because we only have two, maybe three repair options - first they tell you they won't work on LG, but whatever you buy they won't work on that either. Good luck getting a warranty honored on anything. Have decided when I remodel the kitchen, I'm going big - some kind of commercial fridge, as it is clear that consumer grade stuff simply doesn't work. If you are going to spend $3K a pop on a fridge (the prices have gotten crazy too!) and they aren't going to last more than a couple years, just spend the $10K on a commercial model and get your decade+ out of it.

And then there's Bosch, etc... now, I'd like to buy a Bosch, but my current partner doesn't want to spend the money, she likes buying outlet / second-hand / feeling like she got a deal, which is a problem. But - even the top end consumer Bosch is relatively small and I'm not sure the plastic bits are any more durable. I do like the dual compressor system though.

And then there's dishwashers... oh Maytag, how you've fallen thanks to VC/ PE...

author: ipython
title: Declining quality of consumer-grade products – 2009 fridge compressor autopsy
body:
LG and Samsung both have this problem. I suffered from it for years - like clockwork every three months the fan would stop spinning and the fridge would stop working until I took a hair dryer to the built up ice behind the rear panel.

Good news was it encouraged us to clean out our fridge on a regular basis!

I eventually fixed it by ordering a new thermistor and relocating it on the line (I read about it in a service bulletin somewhere)

I also replaced the warming probe at the bottom just in case it was blocking up but I don’t think that was the root cause.

Once I took those actions, the fridge worked great. Unfortunately we now no longer have a clean refrigerator, however.

author: Zelphyr
title: A call to minimize distraction and respect users’ attention (2013)
body:
All I've heard for the past 12+ years is "engagement". The singular focus on that one word to the exclusion of everything else is astounding to me. As if it is some magic incantation on the part of BizDev (or whatever they're called these days) that instantly transmogrifies users into profits.

At one company I worked at, we had a digital product that was part of a suite of services our company provided. It was useful to our customers but it's clear, if you see it, that they want to get in, get done what they need to do, and get out. It's a tool to help them do their jobs and nothing more.

You'd think that simplicity and efficiency would be celebrated. The number of times I heard "engagement" and "gamification" used about that product from the marketing team, however...

Finally I said, "Look. We shouldn't be trying to make our customers spend more time in this product any more than LG does trying to get us to spend more time in our refrigerators." It fell on deaf ears.

I should note that, we didn't make any more money the longer someone spent on that product. There was no advertising model associated with it--it is a per-seat hosted solution. So I never could figure out why our marketing team was all about engagement other than they kept hearing that word said about other digital products and, so, naturally it applies to ours as well and we must do what everyone else is doing!

As if it is some magic incantation on the part of BizDev (or whatever they're called these days) that instantly transmogrifies users into profits.

At one company I worked at, we had a digital product that was part of a suite of services our company provided. It was useful to our customers but it's clear, if you see it, that they want to get in, get done what they need to do, and get out. It's a tool to help them do their jobs and nothing more.

You'd think that simplicity and efficiency would be celebrated. The number of times I heard "engagement" and "gamification" used about that product from the marketing team, however...

Finally I said, "Look. We shouldn't be trying to make our customers spend more time in this product any more than LG does trying to get us to spend more time in our refrigerators." It fell on deaf ears.

I should note that, we didn't make any more money the longer someone spent on that product. There was no advertising model associated with it--it is a per-seat hosted solution. So I never could figure out why our marketing team was all about engagement other than they kept hearing that word said about other digital products and, so, naturally it applies to ours as well and we must do what everyone else is doing!

author: seokgyuhan
title: Add thinqconnect-mcp server
body:
## Description
This PR adds the Official ThinQ Connect MCP Server to the server list. This server provides comprehensive integration with LG ThinQ devices, enabling AI assistants to monitor and control smart home appliances through the Model Context Protocol.

## Motivation and Context
The ThinQ Connect MCP Server fills a gap in smart home device integration for MCP-compatible AI assistants. It provides:

- **Device Management**: Query and control 27+ different LG home appliances
- **Status Monitoring**: Real-time device status and profile information
- **Device Control**: Execute commands like temperature control, power on/off, mode changes
- **Official SDK Integration**: Built on LG ThinQ API and Python Open SDK

### Key Features
- **4 Core Tools**:
  - `get_device_list`: Retrieve all connected ThinQ devices
  - `get_device_status`: Get real-time device status
  - `get_device_available_controls`: Query device capabilities
  - `post_device_control`: Execute device control commands

title: Refrigerator options, toggles, and states appear to do nothing.
body:
<!-- You must use the issue template below when submitting a bug -->

**Describe The Bug:**

• Refrigerator Door status says closed all the time, even after door is left open for several minutes. (NVM - this just started working after I got the logs)
• Express Cool and Express Freeze toggles do nothing and correspond to nothing in the ThinQ app.
• Water Filter Maintenance does not show up anyplace in Home app... not as a tile and not as a sensor.  However, it shows up in Homebridge and always shows "75", whatever that means.  (EDIT:  After a few days, this is now showing 67, so apparently it mean "remaining life")
• It's unclear what the Eco mode toggle does.  Turning it on/off has no impact on the functions shown in the ThinQ app.
• I have my fridge set to "33" as per the ThinQ app and front panel, but it always shows "34" in the app.  Why is this data wrong?
• Current temp and target temps are always the same.  I think this is an issue with LG as the front display and app only show target temps.  There is no "actual" current temperature shown anyplace.  If it's hidden data, then it's not correct... it's just identical mirror of the target.

**To Reproduce:**

Pair an LG refrigerator.  Activate all the options in the JSON config.

**Expected behavior:**

I expect the information and options to be relevant and correspond to info and options in the ThinQ app.  How can I have toggles that do nothing?  I also expect tiles, or the corresponding information that shows up in Homebridge to also show up in HomeKit someplace.

I have tiles that loosely correspond to Fridge and Freezer temperatures, although I have my fridge set to "33" as per the ThinQ app and front display, it always shows "34" target/actual in Homebridge.  

I also think the tiles should only show target temps because this is all you can see in the app.  The "actual" temps are never correct and only mirror the target.

Refrigerator options, toggles, and states appear to do nothing.
<!-- You must use the issue template below when submitting a bug -->

**Describe The Bug:**

• Refrigerator Door status says closed all the time, even after door is left open for several minutes. (NVM - this just started working after I got the logs)
• Express Cool and Express Freeze toggles do nothing and correspond to nothing in the ThinQ app.
• Water Filter Maintenance does not show up anyplace in Home app... not as a tile and not as a sensor.  However, it shows up in Homebridge and always shows "75", whatever that means.  (EDIT:  After a few days, this is now showing 67, so apparently it mean "remaining life")
• It's unclear what the Eco mode toggle does.  Turning it on/off has no impact on the functions shown in the ThinQ app.
• I have my fridge set to "33" as per the ThinQ app and front panel, but it always shows "34" in the app.  Why is this data wrong?
• Current temp and target temps are always the same.  I think this is an issue with LG as the front display and app only show target temps.  There is no "actual" current temperature shown anyplace.  If it's hidden data, then it's not correct... it's just identical mirror of the target.

**To Reproduce:**

Pair an LG refrigerator.  Activate all the options in the JSON config.

**Expected behavior:**

I expect the information and options to be relevant and correspond to info and options in the ThinQ app.  How can I have toggles that do nothing?  I also expect tiles, or the corresponding information that shows up in Homebridge to also show up in HomeKit someplace.

I have tiles that loosely correspond to Fridge and Freezer temperatures, although I have my fridge set to "33" as per the ThinQ app and front display, it always shows "34" target/actual in Homebridge.  

I also think the tiles should only show target temps because this is all you can see in the app.  The "actual" temps are never correct and only mirror the target.

author: ryenitcher
title: LG ThinQ - Cooktop Missing From Range
body:
### The problem

Currently the LG ThinQ integration exposes Ranges as [Oven][thinq_api_oven] only, for models such as the [LSIS6338FE][lg_lsis6338fe]. This does not match the fact that they are combination devices, and ideally should consist of a [Cooktop][thinq_api_cooktop] and a [Oven][thinq_api_oven]. The official LG ThinQ app breaks down the range into the two components, but the same is not done in the official Home Assistant integration.

Additionally, for the Oven entity that is exposed for the range, the Oven entity is exposed as an Upper Oven, instead of a Lower Oven. This is confusing, as a range generally has the cooktop above the oven, not below it. It is even more confusing in cases where an over-the-range microwave oven is to paired with the range via the automatic exhaust fan setting.

author: gboldy
title: LG ThinQ Washer/Dryer Integration Updated From Current Instructions
body:
**Integration name and link**
LG ThinQ Washer/Dryer

**Your card configuration**

**Dryer**
```
type: custom:timer-bar-card
entity: sensor.dryer_current_status
name: Dryer
active_state:
  - running
  - wrinkle_care
  - initial
  - cooling
pause_state: pause
end_time:
  entity: sensor.dryer_remaining_time
translations:
  power_off: "Off"
debug: false
```

**Washer**
```
type: custom:timer-bar-card
entity: sensor.washer_current_status
name: Washer
active_state:
  - spinning
  - detecting
  - initial
  - reserved
  - soaking
  - running
end_time:
  entity: sensor.washer_remaining_time
translations:
  power_off: "Off"
debug: false
```

**Caveats**

The current guidance around using this integration ([#15](https://github.com/rianadon/timer-bar-card/issues/15#issuecomment-1361079381)) is not relevant to the attributes/entities of my ThinQ Washer/Dryer.  My Devices do not have a "Generic" entity as described in that issue (another user details the same thing [here](https://github.com/rianadon/timer-bar-card/issues/15#issuecomment-2784522217)). 

I was able to get mine working with the above yaml and I think it is the best way after troubleshooting quite a bit. The dryer_remaining_time entity state is a timestamp of when the dryer expects to finish. From what I can tell even if the dryer changes the end time when using the "sensing" feature (or whatever its called) this still updates properly but I haven't fully tested this. 

There is another entity for total_time, but I dont think this one will be useful when the washer or dryer automatically changes its time remaining. I do think there is probably a more efficient way to define active_state but this is what's working for me now.

I'm not sure if the old guidance is outdated or if there is just a difference in devices, so the prior guidance may still be relevant.

It seems like because https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/lg_thinq/climate.py#L131-L135 always sets TARGET_TEMPERATURE_RANGE if the unit supports it (even though it is only supported for auto/heat_cool), some integrations (i.e. versatile thermostat) will send high and low temps, which causes errors to throw when the units are in cool or heat mode.  The temp does end up getting set.

Seems like either only supporting feature TARGET_TEMPERATURE_RANGE when in certain modes or ignoring low/high when not in those modes would solve the problem.

core-2025.6.3

title: LG ThinQ Microwave: Setting light and fan values sequentially results in the first value reverting to its original state in ~500ms
body: ### The problem I just set up an automation to turn on the light and vent fan when a burner on our range turns on. When turning both on in sequential actions, first light and then fan, both will turn on, and then the light will toggle back off after about half a second. Swapping the order of the actions swaps the behavior, so triggering fan and then light results in both turning on, and then the fan turning off after half a second. Similar behavior is observed when turning off, just with states inverted. Adding a 2 second delay in between the 2 actions seems to resolve this. title: Random disconnects on Sony XAV-AX5000 with LG G7 ThinQ
body:
On Sony XAV-AX5000 (wired AA), the unit experiences random disconnects at varying intervals, with varying successes and failures reconnecting without a reboot.

**Hardware:** Sony XAV-AX5000, RasPi Zero 2 W, LG G7 ThinQ@10

**Method:** As per doc. Forget all connections (WiFi, Bluetooth), connect with cable, allow to start. Disconnect, boot Pi, pair Phone with Pi, wait...

**Issue:** After maybe 60-90 seconds after boot, it will become connected without user intervention. It will start happily navigating, playing music, making calls for anywhere from about 5 seconds to about 6 minutes (estimate), then AA will disconnect from head unit when nothing is being interacted with. It does this whether or not audio is playing. Navigating with maps on mute still crashes the connection.

After something like 30 seconds to a minute or 2, AA will reconnect (usually). Sometimes it goes into a loop where the head unit repeatedly displays "USB device not supported" every 5 seconds (and beeps 4 times). Sometimes it needs to be rebooted. This did not happen in this log; it reconnected successfully.

I'm really curious what the logs say about which of the 3 pieces of hardware/software is at fault here. There's a lot of potential points of failure and I'm not familiar enough with the various wired/wireless interaction to interpret the logs.

author: Arno500
title: [feature request] Bluetooth LE advertisements in the Core API
body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### Description

It seems that there is no way currently to send arbitrary Bluetooth LE advertisements from an integration. There could be some badly behaving integrations with something that open, but I also see a lot of benefits. For instance, my LG WebOS TV sometimes puts itself in a deep sleep state that does not respond to wake on LAN (it's connected to WiFi; it could be different when connected with Ethernet via RJ45) but will answer to a specific BLE advertisement for instance from the LG ThinQ app on my phone.
I suppose that a lot of devices are working using only BLE without necessarily pairing, especially when handling "power on" commands.

### Additional context

I currently use this integration for WebOS: https://github.com/albaintor/integration-lgtv and it did not successfully wake up the TV from deep sleep (as expected). I then tried using my phone to wake it up, sniffed the packets on my computer, and checked that it was indeed a `LE Extended Advertising Report` with proprietary manufacturer data (need to check, but probably reverse-able)

author: caitotheonlypotato
title: Adjusting LG Fridge/Freezer temperatures via integration produces strange results v2
body:
### The problem

Freezer temperature can't be changed without affecting the fridge, and fridge can't be changed without affecting the freezer

If I adjust the temperature of the freezer via the integration, the freezer temperature changes as requested almost instantly to the correct new temperature, however the fridge always immediately changes to 6 Celsius from whatever its current temperature is (I presume that's the fridge default).

Likewise, when I change the fridge temperature, the fridge side changes as requested almost immediately, and the freezer temperature also instantly changes to -16 Celsius (I presume that's also the default freezer temperature). 

Basically, the temperature setting I change on the integration DOES change the console on the device and changes are held in the integration (EXPECTED RESULT), but other temperature entities also change to a default setting by themselves (UNEXPECTED/UNWANTED)

If I change the temperatures physically on the fridge then the integration is very slow to record the change, usually I just reload the integration, likewise the door open/close reaction time to the integration is lengthy, however the changes made on the fridge console to propagate to the integration.

I have another LG Fridge Freezer upstairs that changes temperatures just fine via the integration.  I have removed and reinstalled the integration, the problem is repeated.  I tried creating a brand new token as well which also didn't help.  All LG devices detect without issue on re-adding the integration.  All the entities per device reappear  as per what I'd expect to see

This has persisted through core 2025.x.x versions.  This problem report has been requested to be resubmitted if still not working as my device has apparently already been implemented with the new specifications.

The old issue  location is here https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/140834#issuecomment-3017574513

title: Added an oven/range card, updated readme language, and updated fridge card
body:
Made a number of changes, principally driven by the addition of an oven/range card.

These changes include:
- Oven/Range card, including background, icons, card code, and sensor template (needed to clear "unknown" from temp field in the unofficial thinQ integration
- Updating the fridge card to include blank 7segment formatting to match the washer, dryer, and dishwasher style
- Updating readme language to reference both the unofficial and official ThinQ integrations, while adding an example card for the over/range and an updated card for the fridge
- Updating the alignment on the icons on the fridge card and dishwasher card to align turbo, wifi, and lock icons while limiting their collision with numerical fields on small screens

Oven/Range card has been tested with an induction range, and all cards have been tested using the (currently somewhat inferior) official integration. Added these notes to the Readme file as well.

title: Clear Voice Pro mode missing in LG Soundbar integration
body:
### Clear Voice Pro mode missing in LG Soundbar integration

#### The problem
The Home Assistant integration for LG Soundbar does not include the **"Clear Voice Pro"** sound mode. While other modes like **"AI Sound Pro"** and **"Cinema"** are available, **"Clear Voice Pro"** is missing from the list.

Additionally, there seems to be a mismatch in sound mode mappings:
- **"Dolby Atmos" mode in Home Assistant sets "AI Sound Pro" on the soundbar.**
- **"User" mode in Home Assistant sets "Standard" mode on the soundbar.**

This suggests that some sound modes are not correctly mapped or missing.

#### Expected behavior
- The **"Clear Voice Pro"** mode should be available as a selectable sound mode.
- The sound mode mappings should align correctly with the actual modes on LG Soundbars.

#### Steps to reproduce
1. Open the LG Soundbar entity in Home Assistant.
2. Check the list of available sound modes.
3. Notice that **"Clear Voice Pro"** is missing.

#### Proposed solution
- Add **"Clear Voice Pro"** to the list of supported sound modes.
- Verify and correct the mapping of sound modes between Home Assistant and the LG Soundbar API.
- Investigate whether the **LG ThinQ API** or **lgsb.js** library can be used to enhance the integration.

#### References
- **LG ThinQ API (Smart Solution API Developer)**: [https://smartsolution.developer.lge.com/](https://smartsolution.developer.lge.com/)
- **LG Soundbar JS Library (lgsb.js)**: [https://github.com/msloth/lgsb.js](https://github.com/msloth/lgsb.js)
- **LG webOS Audio API (for supported devices)**: [https://webostv.developer.lge.com/develop/references/audio](https://webostv.developer.lge.com/develop/references/audio)

thanks for the otherwise great integration.

author: racoonapps
title: 2nd Heating Circuit for ThermaV
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I have a ThermaV heatpump. It's using 2 circuits, one for radiators and one for floor-heating. I can set both circuits properties (temps) in the Thinq App, but I can only set the temp of the first circuit in the integration. I would like to define the heating curve in NodeRED, but that only works if I can control both circuits.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
It would be nice to be able to set both circuits in the integration, just like in the app.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
An alternative would be to use Modbus for everything, but that comes with a lot of work. I am willing to help extending the integration, but wasn't able to use Thinq App with Mitmproxy so far.

author: ooghes
title: Add energy sensor for LG Washer
body:
The latest LG ThinQ app updated the "Energy monitoring" feature by adding a view on the hourly, daily, weekly and monthly energy consumption of the washer (in Wh or kWh). It also shows the cumulative energy consumption. It's a big improvement compared to older app versions which only showed bars without actual values or legend.

It would be great if the existing Home Assistant integration would be extended with a sensor that shows the cumulative energy consumption on an hourly basis. In doing so, a sensor with state_class "total_increasing" becomes available, allowing Home Assistant to track the hourly/daily/monthly/yearly energy consumption associated with the washer and integrate it in the Energy view.

An alternative would be to add a smart plug in the socket that provides power to the washer, but that would not leverage the built-in functionality offered by the washer.

I'm using an LG washer GC3V708S2 TurboWash 39.

author: iteles
title: Networking our LG washing machine
body:
OK, I know this sounds ridiculous 🙆‍♀️ 

But our LG washing machine has the ability to be wi-fi enabled, with certain functionality being controlled from the [LG ThinQ app](https://www.lg.com/us/discover/thinq/laundry).

Here are the features that I think we could intelligently/usefully use and would therefore warrant the connection to wifi:
+ **Push notifications when washing cycles have been completed** meaning there is no going to check if the cycle is complete yet or clothes forgotten in the washer - this would be useful for our caretaker in the short term and for residents in the longer term once we build this into our home app
+ **Energy monitoring** with reports on the energy consumption of the recently used cycles and monthly averages
+ **Download and program custom cycles** for types of washing specific to `home` uses
+ **Smart diagnosis** - if the machine breaks down, this allows for an initial remote diagnosis of the issue by LG engineers

You can also remotely start washing cycles if washing is already in the drum but I don't see a strong use case for this just yet (as you can easily program the machine to start at the desired time when you put the clothing in - this can be done on the machine itself.


The wi-fi module [is open source](http://opensource.lge.com/osList/list?m=Mc014&s=Sc016) so we could eventually build something ourselves but in the meantime the higher priority before we could do this would be to make sure our network is secure.

author: cinadr
title: [FR] Local MQTT integration
body:
Hi!

I've been searching a solution to control my LG Air Conditioners from openHAB for already a year or more probably. This is the only plugin that exists which can control both v1 and v2 devices without any major issues. I'm very grateful for this and it excites me a lot to achieve my long awaited goal.

Right now it is not possible to control accessories from openHAB with the existing bindings only in reverse direction (control openHAB from Homebridge). The only solution would be to implement all the REST API calls from openHAB for all my ACs but this would not provide instant status updates as well only with some polling probably overloading both openHAB and Homebridge.

So I would like to ask if it would be a great amount of work to implement simple get/set MQTT calls to a local MQTT server for each LG accessory to have control and status updates for any subscribers (eg.: openHAB). There is already an MQTT library there connecting to LG MQTT servers. 

Or is there any other solution that someone is aware of that I missed so far? Any help would be appreciated.

Thank you for this great and unique solution and for the continuous development.

Regards,
Zsolt.

PS.: Just another idea to create an independent solution to translate LG MQTT to local MQTT and make this available to all smart home softwares. This would be the first step toward this. (See e.g.: [Zigbee2MQTT](https://www.zigbee2mqtt.io/) or [ZWaveJS2MQTT](https://zwave-js.github.io/zwavejs2mqtt/#/)).

title: [Air Conditioner] MQTT Reports that don't include objects change Homekit ACState incorrectly. (v2.0.0-beta.4)
body:
I've spent the last two weeks working with Copilot to improve the responsiveness and accuracy of this plugin.  Here are somethings I've learned. 

- Excessive Polling;  Many homebridge apps use multiple, short polling periods that are not necessary.  The LG AC I have with wifi built in uses MQTT messages to report changes in real-time, using Wireshark I was able to see a "heartbeat" for the appliance that can be used to drive update behavior. 

- "Missing" Objects in MQTT - I found this plugin will evaluate missing objects from the MQTT monitoring message. During normal operation the AC only includes objects that change in the MQTT message.   The plugin will evaluate missing objects as a "OFF" when it should only update when the object is present. 

- Fan Speed & Rotation Speed Mapping - This needs work to dynamically map AC fan speeds to Homekit Rotation Speed.  The current method of counting the "sensed" fan speeds is not accurate.  My device does not accurately map its available speeds, the API file suggest 4, the LG ThinQ app shows 3 (Low, Med,High).   This configuration should create a 3 segment Slider (0-100) and map those segments to AC Device controls.  I'm still working with Copilot and my limited experience to resolve this one. 

- Config.json options are not evaluated - "Swing Mode" and "COOLING" do not suppress HomeKit UI options.  Selecting "None" for Swing mode doesn't create the object in the config.json file.   Selecting "COOLING" still shows "heating" in the UI> 

- Unnecessary C to F conversions in the plugin - The plugin can work internally with C values from appliance.  Pass the "unit" to Homekit to drive "display units"> Currently there could be multiple conversions happing in AirConditioner.js

- Implement Filter Maintenance Service - This isn't showing up in HomeKit yet.  data is available in Snapshot from device.  Testing this now. 

- Ensuring the AC appears in the "Home Kit Automation Triggers' as a Sensor with "on" and "off" triggers for related automation. 

- Add the ability to use a Remote sensor to control AC behavior.  - I'm adding an additional MQTT listener to intake temp and humidity data from Broadlink RM 4 sensor.  I am working on a "Smart Auto" function that will use this temp sensor to control the AC - mapping this to  "AUTO" in HomeKit.  Work in progress.   This includes mapping my AC's "ECO" opMode 8 into this plugin so it detects its state correctly.

Smart Kitchen Market Analysis and Latest Trends

The Smart Kitchen refers to a modernized approach to cooking and food preparation that integrates advanced technologies, appliances, and automation to enhance user convenience, efficiency, and connectivity. This market encompasses a wide range of products such as smart refrigerators, connected ovens, smart home assistants, and IoT-enabled cooking gadgets.

The Smart Kitchen Market is expected to grow at a CAGR of 14.5% during the forecast period, driven by factors such as the rising trend of smart homes, increased consumer demand for energy-efficient appliances, and the growing influence of connected devices in everyday life. As consumers seek to simplify their cooking processes and enhance their culinary experiences, manufacturers are innovating to offer solutions that enable remote monitoring and control, personalized cooking suggestions, and integration with other smart home systems.

Latest trends in the Smart Kitchen Market include the incorporation of voice recognition technology, touchless controls for hygiene, and advanced sensors that provide real-time data on food freshness. There is also a rising popularity of meal prepping and recipe management applications that streamline cooking processes. Overall, the Smart Kitchen segment is poised for substantial growth, reflecting changing consumer lifestyles and technological advancements.

**Haier Group**, with about $41 billion in revenue, focuses on tailored solutions and acquiring innovative technologies, enhancing its position in the smart kitchen landscape. The company emphasizes smart home integration, which sets it apart in the competitive landscape.

Overall, the smart kitchen market is projected to reach $38 billion by 2027, with players like Electrolux, BSH, and Midea also contributing to the expansion through extensive product lines and strategic partnerships. The ongoing shift towards smart homes and consumer preference for connected appliances indicates sustained market growth, offering significant opportunities for innovation and revenue generation among these key players.

Consumer interest in sustainability and convenience is fueling investments in smart refrigerators, ovens, and meal management apps. Major players are focusing on interoperability and enhancing user experiences. Future outlook indicates a continued expansion as smart home ecosystems proliferate, positioning the Smart Kitchen market as a pivotal sector in the broader home automation landscape.

Smart Connected Kitchen Appliances Market Analysis and Latest Trends

Smart connected kitchen appliances refer to technologically advanced kitchen devices that integrate Internet of Things (IoT) capabilities, allowing them to communicate with each other and users via smartphones and other smart devices. This category includes smart refrigerators, ovens, dishwashers, and more, designed to enhance convenience, efficiency, and energy management in the kitchen.

The Smart Connected Kitchen Appliances Market is projected to grow significantly, with an anticipated compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 11.4% during the forecast period. This growth can be attributed to increasing consumer demand for convenience, the rise in the penetration of smart home technologies, and growing awareness of energy-efficient appliances. Consumers are increasingly prioritizing features such as remote monitoring, customizable settings, and integration with voice assistants.

Trends in the market include the rise of energy-efficient and sustainable appliances, advancements in artificial intelligence for enhanced user experience, and a growing focus on health and wellness, leading to appliances designed for healthier cooking options. As technology continues to evolve, these smart appliances are expected to become more intuitive, making kitchen management easier and more efficient for consumers worldwide.

Smart Connected Kitchen Appliances Major Market Players

The smart connected kitchen appliances market is a rapidly growing segment driven by advancements in IoT, consumer demand for convenience, and increased focus on energy efficiency. Key players in this competitive landscape include Whirlpool Corporation, Electrolux, Samsung Electronics, LG Electronics, Haier Group, BSH Hausgeräte, Miele & Cie KG, Panasonic, Robam, and Midea.

Whirlpool Corporation has established itself as a leader, innovating in connected appliances to offer seamless integration with consumer lifestyles. The company has seen steady growth, largely attributed to its commitment to smart technologies and sustainability, projecting significant market expansion in the coming years.

Samsung Electronics leads in smart technology integration, particularly with its SmartThings platform. This has broadened its consumer reach, encouraging partnerships with other tech companies. Samsung reported sales revenue of approximately $200 billion, with a strong focus on home appliances driving consistent growth.

LG Electronics emphasizes user experience and connectivity through its ThinQ platform. The company aims to expand its offerings in smart appliances, projecting growth in global market share aligned with increasing consumer preferences for IoT-enabled devices.

Electrolux and Haier Group are also key competitors, focusing on smart features and energy efficiency, and investing heavily in research and development to enhance their product lines. Meanwhile, BSH and Miele concentrate on premium segments with innovative design and features, targeting discerning consumers.

Overall, the smart connected kitchen appliances market is expected to reach approximately $30 billion by 2027, driven by technological advancements and evolving consumer preferences. Companies that leverage smart technologies and sustainable practices will likely witness substantial growth in this competitive landscape.

Major players are investing in innovative features such as remote monitoring and automated cooking solutions. As consumer awareness rises, the future outlook remains positive, emphasizing connectivity, customization, and enhanced user experiences.

With the new update of homepodOS/ios 15.4 there have been a few bugs I have encountered.

Yes

Yes

Yes

title: Device list doesn't return Washer
body:
I have 3 SmartThinQ devices (Dishwasher, Washer and Dryer).
Dishwasher and Dryer are returned in the device list but Washier is, for whatever reason, is missing.

I've debugged it as far as I could and it looks like the data returned from POST to device\deviceList just doesn't contain the Washer for some reason. The washer is on the same account and works fine in SmartThinQ app.

I've seen recent mention on HA forum of LG changing their API endpoints.
So, perhaps, there is another API endpoint that could possibly be used instead of device\deviceList to get the list of devices?
